title: Convert Images to JPG: Background, Size, and Download
description: Convert still images to JPG in your browser. Try a background color and proportional resizing, then verify the output dimensions and file size for upload.
content:
To convert an image to JPG in the browser, open the controls in Image Converter. Choose a still image, set “Output format” to JPG, click “Convert,” then click “Download image.” If the source has a transparent background, choose white or a custom color in Settings.

Choose, convert, and download an image

If you see only “Source” and “Result,” click the “Show controls” icon. Click “Choose image” to select a local file, or drag an image onto the page. Once the Source panel shows the format and pixel dimensions, select JPG from the dropdown. If the form requires only a specific format, leave both maximum dimensions blank and convert the image.

When JPG appears in the Result panel, use “Preview result (opens in a new tab)” to inspect the image, then click “Download image.” To submit the image, select the downloaded file in the attachment field. Use “Copy comparison” to share the format and dimensions with a colleague for verification. To submit an attachment, select the file itself.

If several images have similar names, verify the filename under the Source panel after selecting a file. If you're unsure which image you selected, open the source preview. This helps you compare the source and output for the same image and avoid submitting a different photo from the same batch.

Verify the upload requirements

Read the instructions next to the upload field. Some forms accept only JPG. Others also limit file size and pixel dimensions. Note each requirement and verify it after downloading. Width and height in px refer to pixel dimensions. Size in KB or MB refers to file size. A form can impose both limits.

Upload requirement Conversion setting What to verify after conversion
JPG required Select JPG as the output format Format in the Result panel and the downloaded filename
Maximum width and height in pixels Enter the applicable maximum dimensions in Settings Width and height in the Result panel are within the limits
Maximum file size Convert once, then adjust quality or dimensions if the file is too large Output file size, then the upload result
Transparency must be preserved Select PNG if the recipient accepts it Edges and background in the preview

If the form requires an exact width and height, verify the source image's aspect ratio first. If it differs from the required ratio, crop the image to that ratio in an editor before converting. The converter scales photos proportionally to fit within the specified limits. It leaves both sides of a wide landscape image intact.

Choose a background for PNG to JPG conversion

PNG supports transparency. JPGs generated by the browser have no alpha channel. Transparent logos, stamps with cutouts, and portraits with the background removed all need a background color when converted to JPG. The tool uses white by default. To place the image on a colored page, open “Settings” and set “JPG background” to “Custom color.”

If you don't have a transparent image handy, click “Try a transparent PNG” and enter #E8EEF5 in the background color field to try a light blue-gray background. For a dark slide, export the image with the slide's background color, then look for a visible light outline around the logo. If the recipient accepts transparency, choose PNG to make it easier to change the background later.

Verify file size after converting WebP to JPG

For a still WebP saved from a web page, verify that the Source panel identifies it as WebP, then follow the same steps to export it as JPG. WebP supports lossy and lossless compression and can include transparent areas. Web previews often show the image against the page background. Open the source preview before converting to see whether the edges or corners call for a different background color.

Verify the file size in the Result panel after conversion. The source may already be highly compressed, and re-encoding it can produce a larger file. Google's WebP documentation also gives examples of files growing after transcoding. If the result exceeds the attachment limit, adjust the dimensions or quality for the source image, convert it again, and compare the results.

If someone sends you a screenshot of a web page, look at how much of the screenshot the photo occupies. If the margins contain chat messages, menus, or blank space, crop to the area you need in an editor before converting. Scaling down the full screenshot also shrinks the text and the subject.

Set the maximum width and height

“Maximum width” and “Maximum height” set upper bounds on the output dimensions. If you only have a width requirement, enter just the maximum width. If you fill in both fields, the converter scales the image proportionally to meet the tighter limit. If the source already fits within the limits, it keeps its original dimensions. Leave a field blank to impose no limit on that dimension. A value of zero is flagged as invalid.

Use the built-in transparent sample to verify the behavior. The source is 320 × 200 px. Set the maximum width to 160 and leave the height blank. “Estimated dimensions” at the bottom of Settings will show 160 × 100 px. Close Settings, show the controls again, then click “Convert.” Read the actual output width and height in the Result panel.

Inspect fine details when adjusting quality

JPG encoding quality defaults to 85 and accepts integers from 0–100. In spreadsheet screenshots, inspect decimal points and thin horizontal lines. In photos, look at strands of hair and boundaries between light and dark areas. Compare the source and output previews at the same zoom level. If the image will be printed, also inspect the edges of small text on paper.

If the attachment size limit is tight, convert once at the default quality and note the file size. If it's over the limit and the form allows smaller pixel dimensions, reduce the dimensions and try again. Lower the quality if you need to keep the same dimensions. Change one setting at a time and reverse the last adjustment if the text becomes blurry. Verify the actual output size. The quality value does not indicate the percentage reduction in file size.

Spreadsheet screenshots are a good place to make this comparison. If the recipient only accepts JPG, choose an output with legible text that meets the upload limits. If PNG is also accepted, keep the original format for screenshots with thin lines and small text. Exporting at a higher quality cannot recover details that earlier compression removed.

Renaming a file extension and re-encoding an image

Replacing .png with .jpg at the end of a filename changes only the name. The converter reads the file header to identify the container, then decodes and re-encodes the image. If you give it a plain-text file named as a JPG, you'll see “Choose a still JPG, PNG, WebP or AVIF image.” The format in the Source panel can also help identify a mismatch between the filename and file contents.

After generating the result, the converter verifies the media type and file contents returned by the browser. If the browser falls back to PNG for an unsupported export request, the converter rejects the mismatched result. When sharing the file, select the JPG you downloaded. If an API field expects the image as text, use Image to Base64 to generate the text from the JPG.

Supported inputs and limits

The converter accepts still JPG, PNG, WebP, or AVIF images, one at a time. For an animation or sequence, open it in an application that can play the original, choose the frame you want to submit, and save it as a still image before importing it. If the browser reports that it can't decode the image, open the original in an application that supports it and export a still PNG. Changing the extension and importing it again won't resolve a decoding problem.

The input limit is 16 MiB and the output limit is 64 MiB. Each side can be at most 8192 px, and the image can contain at most 16 million pixels. Width multiplied by height can exceed the total pixel limit even when the file size is within bounds. If the tool reports that the image exceeds the dimension limits on import, open the original in an editor, resize it, save a separate file, and import that file. The maximum width and height in Settings apply after the input passes validation.

One state in Settings can be confusing. Changing the dimensions, background color, or quality clears the previous result. If you see “Not converted,” click “Convert” before looking for the download button. To compare several results, give the downloaded files distinct names, then open them side by side from the folder.

Verify the image before downloading

Photo orientation depends on the orientation information the browser can read. For a photo taken with a phone held vertically, use the result preview to verify that faces and the horizon are oriented correctly. The converter generates the result from decoded pixels and omits the source EXIF data, including capture time and location. If you need to retain those details, keep the original separately and submit the converted copy.

A filename such as transparent-sample-converted.jpg helps distinguish the output from the source. If the preview looks right but the file wasn't saved, open the browser's download list. You can also use “Preview result (opens in a new tab)” and try saving the image from that tab. Once it is saved, reopen the file from the downloads folder and verify that you have the version you need.

Verify the file before submitting

Some submissions require both JPG and a smaller attachment. If you need to get closer to a target file size after conversion, use Image Compressor to verify the size again. Keep the original and the upload copy. If details look blurry, return to the source and adjust the settings to avoid repeatedly exporting an already compressed copy.

For print or display, open the image at its intended delivery size. Text that looks clear at full screen may be hard to read at the size you'll actually use. If you replace the image several times in the same form, verify that the attachment field shows the latest file.

  • Verify the format. The Result panel shows JPG, and the attachment field contains the image you just downloaded.
  • Verify dimensions and file size. Compare them with the recipient's pixel and file size limits, respectively.
  • Inspect transparent edges, orientation, and small text. Make sure the background fits where the image will appear and the small text is legible.
  • Review the form after submission. If it shows a thumbnail, verify that the image and version match the local copy.

faqs.q: Can I keep transparency when converting PNG to JPG?
faqs.a: JPG has no alpha channel. The converter uses a white background by default, and you can choose a custom color in Settings. If the recipient accepts transparent images, select PNG.

faqs.q: Will converting to JPG always make the file smaller?
faqs.a: Verify the actual file size in the Result panel after converting. If it exceeds the attachment limit, lower the quality or reduce the maximum dimensions and try again.

faqs.q: Why can't I convert the image I selected?
faqs.a: Look at the Source panel and the error message. If the input exceeds a limit, choose a smaller still image. If a setting is marked in red, correct that field. If an output option is unavailable, try another browser.
